title: The setting screens for your fixtures
summary: Fixtures in TCG Card Shop Simulator are configured where they stand: the game has a setting screen for prices, for the cashier counter, for card storage shelves and for play tables.
body: Fixtures are configured individually. The game keeps a setting screen per kind of fixture rather than one global menu, which is why what you change depends on what you are standing at.
Prices have a screen of their own. There is a screen for setting an item price, which is why pricing is done at the fixture rather than only at the counter.
The counter has one too. The cashier counter carries its own setting screen, so how the counter works is a local decision rather than a shop-wide one.
Storage shelves are set where they are. Card storage shelves have a setting screen of their own, which is why what a shelf holds is decided at the shelf.
Play tables are numbered. There is a screen for setting a table number, which is why tables are identified individually rather than as one group.

The price screen shows its working. It carries the average cost of what is being priced and the profit on it, along with a card interface for setting the price rather than a bare box, so the number is chosen with what it earns in view.
Selling has a confirmation of its own. There is a confirm screen for selling a shelf, so a fixture is not disposed of by accident.
Naming a table is a screen too. It keeps an input along with a display of what has been typed and the table number itself, which is why a number is confirmed before it is set.
The image beside this entry is the game's own: one of the fixture icons it ships, the ceiling tile sheet a setting screen uses for a ceiling fixture.

What this entry does not tell you: how many fixtures each screen covers, what any setting costs, or whether settings can be copied between fixtures. We have not verified those, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: Setting screens exist per kind of fixture rather than as one global menu.
There is a screen for setting an item price.
The cashier counter has its own setting screen.
Card storage shelves have a setting screen of their own.
Play tables are numbered through their own screen.
Selling a shelf has a confirmation screen of its own.
The price screen carries the average cost, the profit and a card interface for setting the price.
The game ships fixture icons of its own for the setting screens, including one for a ceiling.
The table-number screen keeps an input, a display for that input and the table number itself.
The build ships a sheet of fixture icons in more than one colour variant.
